feedback: Written before this candidate races. Iteration 1 (best, 324.07) is the reference: the widened row (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m at y = 0.04 m) with 12 mm sensors and wheel_track 0.12 m gave oval finish rate 0.70 and oval progress 0.95. Iteration 2 showed that 16 mm sensors collapsed oval finishes to 0.00 (progress 0.59), so the footprint should stay at 12 mm. Iteration 3 showed that wheel_track 0.10 m (with kp scaled to 4.5) cut oval finishes to 0.10 and raised oval oscillation to 0.33. So the shorter track adds yaw gain that the oval cannot take, and I have not built the Integrator's controller around it. In the iteration 1 controller, steering_oscillation on the oval was 0.26 and on the s-bend 0.27, and max_error sat at about 0.064 m on the s-bend and slalom, close to the 0.06 m limit. Mass is the remaining lever for yaw inertia, which is mass times (body_length squared plus body_width squared) divided by 12. It acts on the same turn-response lag without changing the sensor geometry that iteration 2 showed is sensitive. Depending on the next race: if oval finishes stay near 0.7 and oscillation falls to about 0.3 or below, keep mass 0.6 kg. If finishes fall while oscillation rises, the lighter robot is losing grip, so move mass back toward 0.7 to 0.8 kg rather than changing the sensors or track again. Body_width does not move the off-track limit within its allowed range, so I would not spend a run on it.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_size 0.012 m and the widened row (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m at y = 0.04 m), since iteration 1 gave the best raced score and iteration 2 showed 0.016 m cost the oval finishes.

If oval finishes fall and steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 at mass 0.6 kg, try mass 0.7 kg as the midpoint back toward the iteration 1 mass, rather than reducing wheel_track further (iteration 3 showed that hurts the oval).

Do not reduce wheel_track below 0.12 m again. If oscillation is still a limit after the mass result, test a longer wheel_track of about 0.13 m, which lowers yaw gain per unit of wheel differential, and read it against the oval finish rate.
